title: M1-01: Reconcile contracts.md with the layout and flow docs (contracts v1.1)
body:
## Goal

Fold every 'New names' table of the four layout docs and the four flow docs into contracts.md before any code uses those names, and give each conflict in plan section 10 (rows 1–37) one answer: its default, unless the owner changes it in review. contracts.md already carries rows 1, 2 and 24, and the platform flow and the node layout already follow rows 2, 4–7, 12, 20 and 26 (section 10's preface), so for those the PR only fixes the docs that still disagree. The rest include the plugin acting principal (`ExecuteRequest.acting_plugin_id`, no header), worker exit code 4 (`EXIT_EVENT_LOG_UNWRITABLE`) in contracts §9.1 and Python §7.2, reattach order (`Register` before `Hello`), `run_job` with `control`, `LogSink` returning `LogCommit`, `TokenizeChat` (not `Tokenize`), graph node `layout{x, y, collapsed}`, lease reclaim by pinned requests only, a recapture only when the set of hooked points changes and two graph variants per slot, interventions applied through `chat.settings.set` with `lens` and `interventions` arguments, plugin jobs through `follow_up_jobs`, layer placement planned by the server, `gateway.request_logged`, gym tools through `WorkerHostService.CallTool`, `rastai eval test` exit codes (ADR-0020), one data-policy code `RRS-C1009`, timing constants, crate dependency edits, new events and tables, and this plan's own new names (plan section 11). It also writes ADR-0034: sign-in through `rastai open --print-url` and `token.login_code.create`, so the desktop shell never reads owner.token; the shell starts the daemon only through `rastai open --print-url` and passes file paths to the web app as a `#/open?path=` URL fragment, and the web app runs `file.open`; any loopback Host on any port, with Origin equal to `http://` plus Host; a too-open owner.token refuses the start; on restart the node waits for the worker's `WorkerHostService.Register`, checks BLAKE3(token) against `job.json` `job_token_hash` (with pid, `boot_id` and `process_start_ticks`), and only then calls `Hello`. ADR-0034 supersedes in part ADR-0007 decisions 3 and 4, ADR-0006 decision 4 and ADR-0001 decision 5; the PR sets their status lines and closes the pending rows of the ADR index's 'Notes since acceptance' table, which also records the illustration and path fixes to ADR-0004, 0005, 0020, 0029 (the Rust reader is `crates/rastai-formats/src/safetensors/reader.rs`) and 0032 (the daemon-free validator is the local `rastai validate <file>`; `rastai file validate` is the generated, daemon-backed verb for `file.validate`). Superseded names in the layout and flow docs get a one-line pointer in the same PR.

## Files and modules

- `docs/architecture/contracts.md` (a 'v1.1 changes' list at the top)
- `docs/architecture/layout/*.md` (a pointer on each superseded name)
- `docs/architecture/flows/*.md` (a pointer on each superseded name)
- `docs/adr/0034-login-codes-loopback-host-owner-token.md`
- `docs/adr/0007-local-api-security.md` (status line: decisions 3 and 4 superseded in part by ADR-0034)
- `docs/adr/0006-ui-transport-http-only.md` (status line: decision 4 superseded in part by ADR-0034)
- `docs/adr/0001-process-layout.md` (status line: decision 5 superseded in part by ADR-0034)
- `docs/adr/README.md` (the ADR-0034 row; the 'Notes since acceptance' table)

## Acceptance test

Docs-only PR, exempt from the test rule (plan 3.3). Review checklist in the PR: every row of every 'New names' table in the eight docs is either in contracts.md or listed as rejected with its replacement; every row of plan section 10 has one answer; ADR-0034 is in the ADR index, and ADR-0001, ADR-0006 and ADR-0007 point to it.

none

title: M1-06: CI workflows for pull requests and nightly runs
body:
## Goal

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` on pull requests and pushes to main, with jobs `checks`, `dco`, `test-rust-linux`, `test-rust-macos`, `test-rust-windows` (CPU; keeps tier 2 compiling, §28 risk 13), `test-python`, `test-python-macos`, `test-python-windows`, `test-ts` and `test-ts-macos`, each one `just` recipe. The macOS and Windows Python jobs run `just test-python-portable`: the CPU tests of the pure-compute packages `rastai_formats`, `rastai_models`, `rastai_data` and `rastai_train` with `-m 'not posix_only'` (only the packages that exist so far; the smoke test until M1-19). The rule for later tasks: a Python test that needs Unix sockets, flock or `setsid` (the worker protocol tests from M1-37, M1-39 and M1-40 on) carries the `posix_only` marker. Spec §29 and §28 risk 13 ask for CPU tests on macOS and Windows from day one, and path handling and the strict safetensors reader are where portability rots first. `.github/workflows/nightly.yml` on schedule, main only, runs the fuzz targets for 10 minutes each (an empty matrix until targets exist). Caches for cargo, uv and pnpm. The new required jobs join the branch-protection contexts (plan 8.4) in the same PR.
